newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Ken Cowley, who has worked with News Limited for 33 years, will retire in June and will be replaced by Rupert Murdoch's son Lachlan. Cowley's resignation as executive chairman will end his day-to-day involvement in the group, but he will retain his positon as a director of News Limited's global parent, News Corporation. Page 1.

Placing further pressure on Westpac Bank's A$1.4 billion bid for the Bank of Melbourne, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Professor Allan Fels said yesterday the Wallis Report backed the position of the ACCC that regional banks are important for competition. Page 3.

The CSR Group is facing possible industrial action throughout its diversified operations because of a dispute over the signing of salaried staff employment contracts for 23 workers at CSR Humes in Darwin. Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union national secretary John Sutton said rolling stoppages at CSR sites would begin from this week. Page 4.

Plutonic Resources Ltd yesterday announced the new Centenary gold deposit looks set to eclipse the major Bronzewing, Jundee and Nimary discoveries, with details showing it contained at least 2.1 million ounces of gold. The discovery, in the north-east of Western Australia, is a major boost to the Australian exploration industry. Page 23.

ANZ Funds Management National Australia Bank Ltd, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Macquarie Bank Ltd and Mercantile Mutual all face a nervous few days as they wait to hear which of them is the successful bidder for the A$18 billion Axiom Funds Management operation. The deadline for the bid ended yesterday, but analysts do not expect the result to be announced for at least another week. Page 24.

Capral Aluminium Ltd chairman Jeremy Davis said yesterday the scrapping of worldwide agreements between aluminium producers in 1994 has led to a period of possible capped price increases and sharper price falls as a result of over capacity. Capral suffered from a plunge in world aluminium prices last year, with a fall in 1996 profits from A$60.3 million to A$29.4 million. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In moves that make him the likely successor to his father Rupert, Lachlan Murdoch was yesterday announced as the replacement of Ken Cowley as executive chairman of News Limited, the Australian arm of News Corporation. Lachlan's new position acknowledges his successful rise through the ranks of the global media group. Page 21.

Philip Morris Australia chief executive Henry Goldberg predicted yesterday the tobacco industry will be hit with a price war by June which will cost up to A$100 million. Goldberg believes the price war between Philip Morris and rivals Rothmans Australia Ltd and WD & HO Wills Holdings Ltd will occur as a result of Wills' discounting. Page 21.

In a recent meeting with New South Wales Premier Bob Carr, National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus said the Bank would pay more than A$200 million for Axiom, the State-owned A$18 billion funds management business which controls the superannuation assets of New South Wales' public servants. Page 21.

A 16-month legal battle ended in humiliation for petrol giant Mobil Oil Australia yesterday, after the Federal Court found it had unnecessarily cut short the leases of 45 of its service stations franchisees. The decision will cost Mobil A$4 million, as it was ordered to reinstate the franchisees with nine-year leases at no cost to the service station operators. Page 21.

American Express (Australia and New Zealand) senior vice-president John Schaap said yesterday the charge card company was willing to join forces with banks following the recommendations in the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system. American Express and Diners Club are the major winners in the Wallis report, which dilutes the privileged position held by conventional banks in the payments system. Page 23.

Australian Gas Association chief executive Ian Woodward said yesterday investment of at least A$3 billion was at risk because of major delays to gas reform. Woodward said that for major energy projects to go ahead, the implementation of the National Acces Code, a key part of the gas reform process, was urgently required. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Plutonic Resources corporate manager Denis Clarke said yesterday drilling in the past two months at the Centenary deposit in Western Australia had revealed an upgraded resource estimate from 900,000 ounces to 2.1 million ounces. The find lifted shares in Plutonic 25 cents to A$4.85, and ends a five year drought for major West Australian gold discoveries. Page 27.

Ken Cowley will end his 32 years with News Limited on a high, with Super League well on its way. His position now is in stark contrast to this time a year ago, when Justice Burchett of the Federal Court ruled that Super League and News Limited acted dishonestly, damning News Ltd's secrecy and deceit. Page 27.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels gave a strong indication yesterday that the Bank of Melbourne takeover by Westpac Bank may be allowed, when he stated the Commission would assess the future shape of banking when making it determinations. Page 27.

Telstra sources confirmed yesterday the Government-owned telecommunications giant will move to restructure its balance sheet ahead of its partial float later this year, with a proposal to raise up to A$3 billion in debt to be considered on Thursday. The move will result in massive dividends for the Federal Government. Page 29.

New South Wales Gaming and Racing Minister Richard Face disclosed yesterday the State-owned TAB lost A$6.3 million on its aborted automated betting operation in Hungary. The operation would be terminated from yesterday, and Face said the TAB had already written off the losses from the operation. Page 29.

QBE Insurance Group agreed in principle to buy a 74.9 per cent stake in Trade Indemnity Australia (TIAL), indicating its intention to expand into the Australasian trade credit insurance business. QBE will also work with TIAL to develop and market specality credit insurance products. Page 29.
THE AGE

Rupert Murdoch's son Lachlan will step into the shoes of Ken Cowley, who announced his resignation yesterday as the executive chairman of News Limited, which runs the Australasian arm of News Corporation. Twenty-five year old Lachlan will take over the position in June, from a man described by Rupert Murdoch as a "fine executive". Page B1.

While Lachlan Murdoch has taken over as the head of News Limited earlier than expected, questions remain over who will gain the post as the head of News Corporation once Rupert Murdoch resigns. While Lachlan, with seats on the News Corp board and executie committee, is the favourite, his sister Elisabeth is still a strong contender following her success with BSkyB, News Corp's 40 per cent-owned UK satellite television venture. Page B1.

Under what would be one of the biggest infrastructure projects for Australia and Papua New Guinea, United States oil giant Chevron announced plans yesterday to pipe gas from Papua New Guinea's remote southern highlands to Townsville and Gladstone in Queenland. Under the plan, the A$3 billion project would be up and running by the middle of 2001. Page B1.

Victorian Industry Minister Mark Birrell announced yesterday 100 jobs will be created under plans by UCB SA, the Belgian company that supplies the plastic coating for Australian banknotes, to establish a A$50 million plastic-film manufacturing plant at Craigeburn. Page B1.

Ashton Mining hopes to expand its Argyle diamond mine in Western Australia with or without the support of its joint venture partner RTZ-CRA. Currently Argyle is set to cease production by 2003, with the partners currently deciding whether to proceed with an underground mine at the site or to expand the existing open pit. Page B3

After turning its back on a proposed merger with St Barbara Mines, Queensland-based gold producer Mount Leyshon Gold Mines is now reviewing how to use its surplus cash flow. Options being considered include a return to shareholders through dividend payments, the development of another project and funding additional exploration. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
